issue: stalled_section hardcodes "live on master" although the stall record carries `branch` (a trunk/topic-branch custody renders a wrong report line); the PRD and design text mandate this literal
reason: The PRD's 'Custody in the stalled report' output text mandates the literal `- Commits: <range> (<n>) live on master, custody pending` and the design pins it byte-for-byte; a branch-aware line is a spec change, not a defect. Bob filed it as KNOWN with this reason.

issue: _refresh_block scans 20 head lines while frontmatter._HEAD_LINES is now 22: a block closing on line 21-22 parses before the refresh, then gets a second block prepended and its original keys drop out of frontmatter.parse (needs 19+ keys; design-specified bound)
reason: Design-specified: § Hold PRD refresh says the refresh treats a block that does not close within the first 20 lines as no block, and _HEAD_LINES moved to 22 precisely so a block that closed within 20 still parses after the two custody keys are added. Reachable only with 19+ frontmatter keys, which no PRD in this repo has. Bob filed it as KNOWN with this reason.

issue: records and custody import each other (`from . import custody` / `from . import records`); works only because attributes are accessed lazily inside functions
reason: The design contract places the record_defer calls inside custody.record_critical and the record_critical call inside records.do_stall (§ cli/records.py changes, step 4b); the module-level imports resolve because every attribute is read inside a function body, and every suite imports both modules in both orders. Documented shape, not a defect. Bob filed it as KNOWN.

issue: Guard worst case exceeds its 10s hooks.json timeout: up to 8 candidate cwds each running resolve_toplevel (5s) plus marker_from_locator (5s)
reason: Reaching it needs eight literal cd candidates in one command, each inside a repository whose git hangs for the full 5s; the common path is one `in` check and a real push costs at most two 5s git calls, which the design § Risks documents as the accepted cost. resolve_toplevel is memoized per path. Bob filed it as KNOWN with this reason.

issue: custody.marker_entry() is built twice with identical inputs in the do_stall step-4b path (once inside custody.record_critical, again in records._record_stall_custody right after) instead of threading the single built entry through; harmless since the builder is pure, but redundant
reason: record_critical's signature is the design's verbatim contract (keyword-only inputs, returns int | None); threading the entry through means changing that interface (a new parameter or a dict return) to save one pure five-key dict build. Both call sites already share the single builder (the cycle-1 finding that mattered); the residual duplicate call is not worth an interface change. Alice rated it Low and harmless.
